title: Preemptive GPU Warm-Drain TODO
content:
Notes to self — warm-drain / preemptive GPU maintenance run

Context:
- Running a small warm-drain across a subset of prod-gpu pool to validate eviction behaviour after the new kube-scheduler patch. Not a full maintenance; target low blast radius.
- Goal: exercise KV-cache restore, confirm pod reschedule latency < 45s for most small-chat pods, ensure autostart of background checkpointing processes.

Quick plan (today, short window 09:30-10:30 PT):
1) Pick nodes (5 nodes, spread across racks 3/4/7) 
   - Candidate nodes: gpu-prod-03a, gpu-prod-08b, gpu-prod-15c, gpu-prod-22a, gpu-prod-27d
   - Confirm SRE ok with rack choices (avoid racks with boot storms last week)
2) Preflight checks (must be green):
   - infra/monitoring alerts: none (check /alerts/gpu and /alerts/pod-latency)
   - node readiness: kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o wide -> nodes Ready
   - disk pressure: df -h on each node; < 80%
   - NV driver versions: nvidia-smi check, match expected 535.*
3) Run warm drain command (drain but allow evictions):
   - command: kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60 --timeout=600s
   - pace: start next node 6m after observing pod evictions + reschedules stable for 2m
4) Observe and collect metrics:
   - pod reschedule time (from eviction event to pod Ready) -> watch kubectl get pods -w and prometheus metric pod_startup_time_ms
   - nvml GPU memory share distribution (nvidia-smi dmon or DCGM)
   - network attach timeouts (CNI logs: /var/log/cni/cni.log)
   - model-serving tail logs for first 3 rescheduled pods per node (grep for "kv-cache restored" or "started checkpoint")

Commands / snippets I keep using (paste here for quick run):
- list candidate nodes: kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}\n'
- check driver: kubectl debug node/<node> -- image=nvcr.io/nvidia/k8s-utils:latest -- nvidia-smi -L
- watch pod reschedule: kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide --field-selector=status.phase!=Running -w
- prometheus quick query: sum(rate(kube_pod_container_status_ready[1m])) by (pod)

Failure modes to watch for (if any one happens -> abort and uncordon all):
- >10% of evicted pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff after 10m
- Any spike in 5xx responses from the API gateway >1 minute sustained
- Node-side kubelet OOM or kernel OOPS messages in dmesg
- CNI plugin errors: repeated "failed to set up" for >5 pods

Post-run checklist (immediate):
- Revert if unstable: kubectl uncordon <node> and watch pods come back (some pods might remain Terminating, follow up)
- Upload logs: infra/gpu-warmdrain/<date>/ node-logs.tar.gz -> S3 (prefix: s3://redwood-infra-wip/gpu-warmdrain/2026-03-13/)
- Fill quick postmortem snippet and tag PLAT-3421 with run results

Manual notes / observations to jot down during run:
- pod startup latencies (sample): chat-small-2: 28s, reranker-batch-1: 47s, embedder-rt: 14s
- observed nvtop spikes on gpu-prod-08b at eviction moment, memory freed slower than expected (~6s)
- CNI attach on gpu-prod-15c logged 3 timeouts - raised to SRE for follow-up

Open questions / TODOs beyond today:
- Should we increase default drain timeout from 600s to 900s for stateful sidecars that checkpoint? Follow-up: open a small RFC describing tradeoffs.
- Need a synthetic test that simulates KV cache warmup: create a lightweight job that repeatedly calls /restore endpoint and measures latency; place as a CI job under infra/tests/kv-warmup.
- Investigate host-level overlay config: last week's packet drops correlate with kernel update on 4 nodes; schedule a window to test older kernel binary fallback.

Personal reminders (for handoff):
- If I leave mid-run, @Meera will continue — ping channel #ops-gpu and prefix messages with "WARM-DRAIN".
- Keep phone on for 20m after uncordon in case SRE page triggers.

Random implementation note (script idea):
- small bash helper to run paced drains:
  for n in "$@"; do
    kubectl cordon "$n"
    kubectl drain "$n" --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60 --timeout=600s || { echo "drain failed $n"; kubectl uncordon "$n"; exit 1; }
    sleep 360 # 6 minutes
  done

Last-run quick summary (from run on 2026-02-20):
- 4 nodes drained, average reschedule 33s, one pod stuck due to local disk dependency -> fixed by adding emptyDir fallback.
- No major gateway errors.

End note: keep this lightweight. This doc is a scratchpad; if we formalize the warm-drain procedure, move a copy to shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/playbooks/warm-drain-runbook.md

-- Amit
